title: Little Office of S. Peter, Prince of the Apostles
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Petri laudes extollamus, Nos romanae quotquot stamus Castris sub ecclesiae,
blocks.english:
Let us exalt the praises of Peter,
All of us who stand
Beneath the camp of the Roman Church,

blocks.source: Alme claviger coelorum, Rudem ne despexeris chorum Rhytmo textum simplice!
blocks.english:
Kindly bearer of the keys of heaven,
Despise not our rough choir,
Woven in simple rhythm!

blocks.source: Nam sic belle concordantes Qui virtutes tam praestantes Sat laudari valeant!
blocks.english:
For how could virtues so excellent,
So beautifully in harmony,
Be praised enough?
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Qui ... valeant” is grammatically compressed; the question about praising the harmonious virtues is provisional.

blocks.source: Amor, timor, mens sincera, Zelus, fides, spesque vera Pari melo consonant;
Est in Petro, quam addidicit Princeps, quae in servo gliscat, Adest et humilitas,
blocks.english:
In Peter there is humility also,
Which the prince learned
That it might flourish in the servant,
blocks.editorialNote: “quam addidicit Princeps, quae in servo gliscat” is compressed; the relation of prince, servant and humility is provisional.

blocks.source: Christum sequi hic cunctator, Ab hoc fundere peccator Justas discet lachrymas.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “hic cunctator ... Ab hoc” is compressed; its exhortation is rendered provisionally.

blocks.source: Illic proximum juvare, Deum unice amare: Et, quos mundus detinet,
Fluxa quaevís aspernari, Nudos Christum insectari Petrus nos erudit.
blocks.english:
Peter teaches to despise all passing things,
And stripped of them
To follow Christ.

blocks.source: ℣. Simon Joannis, diligis me? etiam.
blocks.english: ℣. Simon, son of John, dost thou love Me? Yea.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, tu scis, quia amo te.
blocks.english: ℟. Lord, Thou knowest that I love Thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis s. Petre apostole,
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Peter the Apostle,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus qui b. Petro apostolo tuo, collatis clavibus regni coelestis, ligandi atque solvendi pontificium tradidisti: concede, ut intercessionis ejus auxilio a peccatorum nostrorum nexibus liberemur. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre etc.
blocks.english: O God, who, bestowing the keys of the heavenly kingdom upon blessed Peter Thy Apostle, didst entrust to him the pontifical power of binding and loosing, grant that through the help of his intercession we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. Who livest and reignest with God the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super etc.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The opening “Tu es Petrus, et super etc.” is abbreviated in this office. No full counterpart is printed here; no external text is imported.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Hunc piscantem, Piscatoris Ad capturae dignioris Opus traxit Gratia;
Nam qui iubet sic piscari, Pisces vitae vult servari, Quos prehendant retia,
Unde Petrus se vocantis Nullum Christi tunc patrantis Signum vel prodigium, Voci cedit, verbo credit, Sequi iussus, mox obedit, Quo vocaret servulum,
blocks.english:
Hence Peter yields to the voice
Of Christ who calls him,
Though then working no sign or wonder;
He believes the word,
Commanded to follow, he soon obeys,
Wherever He would call His little servant,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed relative clauses about Christ’s calling are compressed; no omitted miracle is added.

blocks.source: Vanis praefert veritatem, Linquit rete, linquit ratem, Quin relinquit omnia;
Et, o felix Bar-Jona Pro his Christus tibi bona, Regna spondet supera:
Dumque calcas undas maris, Te nutantem, ne mergaris, Fida manu detinet,
Fidem quatit dum tempestas Ejus alma vim potestas Procellarum cohibet.
blocks.english:
While the tempest shakes faith,
His kindly power restrains
The force of the storms.

blocks.source: Ant. Clamavit Petrus: Domine salvum me fac; et JESUS extendens manum apprehendit eum.
blocks.english: Ant. Peter cried: Lord, save me; and Jesus, stretching forth His hand, took hold of him.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed incipit repeats the specified prayer group from this office only. Printed abbreviations and source-reading warnings in the target remain.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super etc.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The opening “Tu es Petrus, et super etc.” is abbreviated in this office. No full counterpart is printed here; no external text is imported.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Mota Christi quaestione, Brevi claudit sub sermone Fidem necessariam;
Hunc personam dicit unam, Sed naturae opportunam Simul dat distantiam, Carni scire, quod negatum, Sibi Cephas revelatum Dia profert diphthera
blocks.english:
He declares Him one Person,
But at the same time gives
The fitting distinction of nature;
What flesh is denied to know,
Cephas, to whom it was revealed, declares
[The printed “Dia ... diphthera” is uncertain.]
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Dia profert diphthera” is uncertain. The two-nature distinction is retained as printed, without supplying a missing formula.

blocks.source: Super quo, perennatura, Petra tanquam super dura Conditur Ecclesia,
blocks.english:
Upon whom the Church,
Destined to endure, is founded
As upon a hard rock,

blocks.source: Quin et sorte, ut miranda Petre liges, quae liganda, Rata sint, quae solveris
Christus claves tibi credit, Quibus Coeli porta cedit, Pandas, vel occluseris,
Quodque hic est implicatum, Summus Judex et ligatum Super astra voluit;
Quae haec dignitas dicenda? Alta plane et tremenda, Quam vix sensus percipit.
blocks.english:
What must this dignity be called?
Truly lofty and dreadful,
Which understanding scarcely grasps.

blocks.source: Ant. Quodcunque ligaveris super terram, erit ligatum et in caelis, et quodcunque solveris super terram, erit solutum et in caelis.
blocks.english: Ant. Whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose upon earth shall be loosed also in heaven.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super etc.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The opening “Tu es Petrus, et super etc.” is abbreviated in this office. No full counterpart is printed here; no external text is imported.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Transformantis se Messiae, Moysis simul, et Eliae Frueris colloquio, Censens hic manere gratum, Semper hoc si foret datum Esse in consortio;
At, quid erit, Majestatem, Quid aeternis Deitatem Contemplari gaudiis?
blocks.english:
But what shall it be
To contemplate the Majesty and the Godhead
In everlasting joys?

blocks.source: Ubi, junctis tot Beatis, Una dies claritatis Mille praestat saeculis,
blocks.english:
Where, joined to so many blessed ones,
One day of brightness
Surpasses a thousand ages,

blocks.source: Petrus posthac Salvatori Fidus comes, optat mori Pariter cum Domino;
Zelus calcar est amoris, Sed et casus est timoris Jugis admonitio,
Tibi Christus eventurum Quem praedixit, ne securum Obruat fiducia,
Sed prostratum Patientis Anxiumque Resurgentis Erigat memoria.
blocks.english:
But that the memory of Him who suffered
May raise thee when cast down,
And of Him who rose again when anxious.

blocks.source: Ant. Simon, Simon, Satanas expetivit vos, ut cribraret sicut triticum: Ego autem rogavi pro te, ut non deficiat fides tua.
blocks.english: Ant. Simon, Simon, Satan has sought you that he might sift you like wheat; but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super etc.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The opening “Tu es Petrus, et super etc.” is abbreviated in this office. No full counterpart is printed here; no external text is imported.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Ter negavit quod peccavit, Kursus Amor expiavit, Triplex et Confessio:
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Kursus”; “again” is a conjectural reading.

blocks.source: Hinc sequutos delinquentem Iam et Petrum poenitentem Sequi iubet ratio.
blocks.english:
Hence reason bids those who followed
The sinner now also
To follow Peter penitent.

blocks.source: Sed quam Christus carum gregem Det pascendum, prius legem Charitatis ponderat,
Amat Petrus, contestatur, Amat: Sed haec tremens satur, Galli dum meminerat,
blocks.english:
Peter loves; he bears witness that he loves,
But speaks these things trembling,
As he remembers the cock.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “haec tremens satur” is defective; the trembling/confession reading is provisional.

blocks.source: Auro carens et argento, Posthac claudum in momento Membris donat validis,
Dat Aeneae sanitatem, Hinc et inde sospitatem Aegis fert, et miseris,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Aegis” is irregular; “to the sick” is provisional.

blocks.source: Quin ad funus dum Tabithae Venit, suis reddit vitae Precibus officia.
blocks.english:
Nay, when he comes to Tabitha’s burial,
By his prayers he restores
The functions of life.

blocks.source: Sola umbra decumbentes Porro sanat, et languentes Ope curat coelica.
blocks.english:
His shadow alone further heals
Those who lie sick,
And cures the languishing with heavenly help.

blocks.source: Ant. Augebatur credentium multitudo, ut in plateas ejicerent infirmos, qui veniente Petro saltem umbra illius liberantur ab infirmitatibus suis.
blocks.english: Ant. The multitude of believers increased, so that they carried the sick into the streets, who, as Peter came, were delivered from their infirmities by at least his shadow.
blocks.editorialNote: The relative construction “qui ... liberantur” is defective; the printed shadow narrative is retained in sense.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super te.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon thee.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints the short “Tu es Petrus, et super te.” It is translated as printed rather than silently completing it.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Strictam gregis curam gerit, Defraudantes gravi ferit Coniuges supplicio,
Fraudes damnant et fallaces, Quo Divina in mendaces Mox descendit ultio.
blocks.english:
They condemn frauds and deceivers,
Whereby divine vengeance
Soon descends upon liars.

blocks.source: Sed et capto dans custodes Iners fallitur Herodes Suo cum satellite,
Quippe vincis relaxatus, Jam it Petrus liberatus, Fido cinctus Comite,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “vincis” is irregular; “bonds” is provisional.

blocks.source: Magus utque Petrum odit, Sic Simonem Petrus prodit Turpi de flagitio;
Nam volare hic dum quaerit, Gravi palam lapsu perit Asfectante Populo;
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Asfectante”; the crowd looking on is a conjectural reading.

blocks.source: Unde Nero insfendescens, Magi lapsum miserescens Petro fert judicium,
blocks.english:
Hence Nero, growing angry
And pitying the magician’s fall,
Passes judgment upon Peter,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “insfendescens” is defective; the angry Nero reading is provisional.

blocks.source: Ut in Crucem sublevetur, Quo Magistrum imitetur Pari trabe pendulum.
blocks.english:
That he be raised upon a cross,
So as to imitate his Master,
Hanging upon a like beam.

blocks.source: Ant. Cum esses junior cingebas te, et ambulabas, ubi volebas: Cum autem senueris, extendes manus tuas, et alius te cinget et ducet, quo tu non vis.
blocks.english: Ant. When thou wast younger, thou didst gird thyself and walk where thou wouldst; but when thou shalt grow old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee and lead thee where thou wouldst not.

blocks.source: Vers. et Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Verse and prayer as above.

blocks.source: Tu es Petrus, et super te.
blocks.english: Thou art Peter, and upon thee.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints the short “Tu es Petrus, et super te.” It is translated as printed rather than silently completing it.

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Dumque Petro Crux paratur, Crucifigi hic laetatur Equidem cum Domino,
Sed eodem situ lignum Haud subire censens dignum Nisu rogat ultimo:
blocks.english:
But judging himself unworthy
To undergo the wood in the same position,
With a final effort he asks

blocks.source: Pedibus ut elevatis, Inque terram declinatis Vertice et manibus
blocks.english:
That with his feet raised,
And his head and hands
Turned down toward the earth,

blocks.source: Cruci suae alligetur, Ne Magistro par tractetur Servus et Discipulus,
blocks.english:
He be bound to his cross,
Lest the servant and disciple
Be treated as equal to the Master.

blocks.source: Sic mi Petre! versa cruce Coelum scandis; Isthac duce Fac et nos id scandere,
blocks.english:
Thus, my Peter, by an inverted cross
Thou dost ascend to heaven; by its guidance
Grant that we too may ascend there.

blocks.source: Tuo gregi fores pande Gnaro, clavium hoc grande Tibi jus competere,
Oves, tuo quas ovili Hic in terris haud exili Cura enutviveras, Christo tandem Redemptori Primo redditas Pastori, Duc ad Agni nuptias,
blocks.english:
The sheep whom in thine earthly fold
Thou didst nourish with no small care,
At length restored to Christ the Redeemer,
The first Shepherd,
Lead to the marriage of the Lamb.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “enutviveras” is irregular; “didst nourish” is provisional.

blocks.source: Ant. Amen, Amen dico vobis, quia ego sum ostium ovium, per me si quis introiverit, salvabitur, ingredietur et egredietur, et pascua inveniet.
blocks.english: Ant. Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep; if anyone enters through Me, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and find pastures.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis S. Petre Apostole.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint Peter the Apostle.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Mitissime ac Clementissime Deus, qui S. Petrum ex pauperculo piscatore, tuum in terris Vicarium, atque Apostolorum Principem constitutisti, eumque post grave negationis peccatum propitiis tamen respexisti oculis, et ad amarissimam poenitentiam commovisti. Oro te per intimum ejus amorem, et ferventissimas lachrymas, concede mihi gratiam tuam exuberantem, ut voluntati tuae me totum subternens, vocationi meae semper satisfaciam, et in petra Catholicae fidei immote persistere, Te summum Bonum meum in prosperis et adversis, super omnia amem, atque peccata mea contra Divinam Majestatem tuam commissa, vero, et profundissimo dolore plangam, donec tandem in coelis gaudio petrui merear sempiterna; Qui vivis et regnas Deus in saecula saeculorum, Amen.
blocks.english: Most meek and most merciful God, who didst make Saint Peter, from a poor fisherman, Thy Vicar upon earth and Prince of the Apostles, and after his grievous sin of denial didst nevertheless look upon him with gracious eyes and move him to most bitter repentance, I pray Thee through his intimate love and most fervent tears: grant me Thine abundant grace, that, submitting myself wholly to Thy will, I may always fulfil my vocation, remain unmoved upon the rock of the Catholic faith, love Thee, my supreme Good, above all things in prosperity and adversity, and lament with true and deepest sorrow my sins committed against Thy divine Majesty, until at length I may deserve to enjoy everlasting joy in heaven. Who livest and reignest, God, world without end. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “subternens,” an irregular infinitive “persistere,” and “petrui ... sempiterna.” The English clauses are provisional and the Latin remains unchanged.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. Seven hours are printed, without Lauds. Five verse-and-collect references expand the Matins group. Opening “Tu es Petrus” incipits remain short because this office does not supply their full text. The different full Compline prayer remains distinct, and the source’s Simon Magus narrative is preserved.
